title: Graph isomorphism in quasipolynomial time on a single-tape Turing machine
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Babai's quasipolynomial-time algorithm for graph isomorphism, without the classification of finite simple groups, carried down to Turing machines. There is a single-tape Turing machine (Mathlib's Turing.TM0) that decides whether two simple graphs on n vertices, given in a fixed encoding, are isomorphic within 2^(c (floor(log2 n) + 1)^8) transitions, and another that within the same bound outputs either "not isomorphic" or an isomorphism τ together with generators of a subgroup whose left coset by τ is exactly the set of all isomorphisms. The algorithm (Luks's framework, Schreier–Sims, Weisfeiler–Leman refinement and the Design Lemma, Split-or-Johnson, local certificates and Babai's recursion, with Pyber's analysis in place of the classification), its cost in an executed cost model, and its compilation to multi-stack and then single-tape machines are all proved in Lean.
